# Plan-Limit Signal Reference

How a recognized plan-limit `403` renders under each output format, the structured envelope element that names the gating feature, and the exit code it carries.

## Overview

Plan-Limit Signal is the rendering half of plan-limit signalling. [Feature-Gate Recognition](feature-gate-recognition.md) does the recognizing; this capability turns a recognized gate into operator-facing output.

It adds **no flag and no command**. It changes only the wording and envelope content of an existing `403` failure, and only when that `403` came from a known plan-gated operation. Every other failure — and every non-recognized `403` — renders byte-for-byte as it did before.

The signal reuses the `--output` flag and the four format values from [output format selection](output-format-selection.md): `full`, `compact`, `json`, `yaml`.

## Firing Conditions

The signal fires only when both hold:

1. The failure is a `403`.
2. Feature-Gate Recognition matches the failed operation to a registered plan-gated row.

A `403` from any other operation, and any non-`403` from a gated operation, render exactly as they do without this capability.

## Human Formats (`full`, `compact`)

Channel and shape are unchanged from [output-aware failure rendering](../guides/output/how-to-choose-an-output-format.md): stderr carries a single line of the form `<cause> — <next step>`. stdout stays empty.

For a recognized plan-limit `403`, the cause and next step are the gate-aware ones, so the line names the gating feature and frames it as a possibility:

```
this operation requires the Premium async proposals feature, which your organization's plan may not include; a 403 may instead mean your identity lacks permission — verify your organization's plan includes Premium async proposals, or that your identity has permission for this operation
```

The gate name appears in the cause prose. The human line has no distinct field for it — the distinct element exists only in the structured envelope.

### Wording Templates

| Part | Template |
|---|---|
| Cause | `this operation requires the <feature> feature, which your organization's plan may not include; a 403 may instead mean your identity lacks permission` |
| Next step | `verify your organization's plan includes <feature>, or that your identity has permission for this operation` |

`<feature>` is the recognized gate's display name. No plan name, price, or upgrade URL is ever added — the display name is the only added specific.

## Structured Formats (`json`, `yaml`)

The unified error envelope carries one **additional** field, `feature`, alongside the existing fields.

| Field | Type | Presence | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | always | the diagnostic's cause — the possibility-framed plan-limit cause naming the gate |
| `next_step` | string | when present | the recovery action — the "verify the plan includes `<feature>`" wording |
| `feature` | string | **only for a recognized plan-limit `403`** | the gating feature's display name, as its own parseable key — not folded only into `message` (though `message` also names the gate) |
| `kind` | string | always | the category token — `permission`, unchanged |
| `status` | integer | non-2xx | `403` |
| `body` | object / array | when the API returned a valid-JSON body | the raw `403` body verbatim |

Field declaration order is `message` → `next_step` → `feature` → `kind` → `status` → `body`. JSON preserves it; YAML emits keys alphabetically. Rely on the keys, not their order.

`feature` is omitted when empty, so **every non-plan-limit failure renders the exact prior envelope, byte-stable**. The key appears only for a recognized plan-limit `403`.

### Example

`glassfrog proposal propose prp_0123 --output json`, advancing a draft on a non-Premium organization:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "this operation requires the Premium async proposals feature, which your organization's plan may not include; a 403 may instead mean your identity lacks permission",
    "next_step": "verify your organization's plan includes Premium async proposals, or that your identity has permission for this operation",
    "feature": "Premium async proposals",
    "kind": "permission",
    "status": 403,
    "body": { "type": "about:blank", "title": "Forbidden", "detail": "Forbidden" }
  }
}
```

## Gate Display Names

The operator-facing diagnostic uses human-prose display names, distinct from the machine-legible gate names in [Feature-Gate Recognition](feature-gate-recognition.md#gate-kinds).

| Gate | Display name |
|---|---|
| `none` | *(empty — no gate)* |
| `premium-async-proposals` | `Premium async proposals` |
| `ai-integration` | `AI Integration` |

The mapping is total: every gate kind has a display name. Adding a gate kind without one fails loudly rather than rendering broken prose. If a gate is somehow recognized without a display name, the generic permission diagnostic is rendered instead.

## Error Reference

| Failure | `full` / `compact` | `json` / `yaml` | Exit code |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recognized plan-limit `403` (gated operation) | gate-aware cause and next step on stderr, naming the feature and framing possibility | envelope on stdout with `kind: permission`, `feature: <name>`, `status: 403`, and `body` when valid JSON | `4` |
| Non-recognized `403` (non-gated operation) | the generic permission cause and next step on stderr | the prior envelope — **no `feature` key** | `4` |
| Non-`403` from a gated operation (`422`, `412`, …) | that status's usual wording | the prior envelope — **no `feature` key** | per status (`3` / `7` / …) |

### Exit Code Is Unchanged

A recognized plan-limit `403` is still a permission error → exit `4`, identical across all four formats. This capability refines wording and adds the `feature` element; it never remaps the category or the code. See [exit code convention](exit-code-convention.md).

Rendering and exit code both derive from a single normalized diagnostic, so the rendered facts, the category, and the gate name cannot disagree.

### Secret Safety

No API token or auth header appears in any rendered plan-limit failure. The cause and next step are static gate-aware templates plus the gate display name, and the envelope carries only response-side facts.

## Possibility, Never Certainty

The wording never asserts the plan is insufficient and never tells the caller to upgrade, because a genuine permission `403` on a gated operation is indistinguishable from a plan gate. The next step is to **verify**, not to upgrade.

## Scripting

`glassfrog proposal propose <prp-id> --output json` yields a parseable envelope on which a caller can branch on `error.feature` to detect a plan limit programmatically. The exit code remains the authoritative failure signal.
